cohort_total_n_excerpt: A case control study was carried out among 105 subjects (case n=35, control n=70), matched for age and ethnicity.
reason: This case-control study evaluated prostate cancer occurrence without reporting stage, grade, high-risk, metastatic, lethal, or another aggressive subtype endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Intake of tomato sauce of more than 2.24 g/d (25th percentile), papaya more than 22.7 g/d (50th percentile) and oranges more than 19.1g/h (50th percentile) reduced prostate cancer risk by 7.4 (Adjusted OR 7.4 (95% CI 1.17-46.8)), 2.7 (adjusted OR 2.75 (95% CI 1.03-7.39)) and 2.6 times (adjusted OR = 2.6 (95% CI=1.01-6.67)), respectively (p < 0.05 for all parameters).
estimate_classifications.reason: The papaya estimate is for prostate cancer generally. The stored estimate is an inversion of the abstract's reported orientation, but that does not change its endpoint classification.
